A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with matching methods and retained experimental results despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original task-addition experiments, fine-tuning ablations, disentanglement measurements, and appendix single-task results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds language-task results, efficiency measurements, a kernel-behavior diagnostic, and coefficient sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Despite the change from 'linear layers only' to 'attention modules only,' v1 Figure 2 and v2 Figure 4 specify the same trainable Q, K, V, and output projection weights. Scaled task-vector addition remains unchanged; no substantive change to the proposed training or inference procedure is documented.

E1.justification: v2 adds language evaluation on seven GLUE tasks: CoLA, MNLI, MRPC, QQP, RTE, SST2, and STSB. This substantially extends the empirical scope beyond the eight retained visual classification datasets.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 3 adds an explicit comparison using post-hoc linearized versions of full-model and attention-only fine-tuning, absent from v1's reported comparisons. The principal task-addition comparators remain non-linear fine-tuning and NTK linearization; the new GLUE comparison reuses them.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Flan-T5-base evaluation, a post-hoc linearization test, and an explicit coefficient sweep. It also revises ablation settings (3)–(4) from attention linear layers to attention plus MLP weights, and inserts coefficient scaling into the normalized-accuracy numerator and denominator. These reported changes do not establish reruns of the unchanged vision tables; the existing CLIP training schedule remains intact.

E4.justification: The new kernel-behavior diagnostic in Figure 3 tests agreement between non-linear and post-hoc models. Appendix B.3/Figure 9 adds accuracy sensitivity to the mixing coefficient. The four-way ablation remains numerically unchanged but now explicitly addresses MLP inclusion. The cosine-similarity analysis is retained, relocated to Appendix B.4.

E5.justification: v2 specifies initialization seed 42 for the added GLUE experiments; v1 gives no corresponding seed information. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. This is a seed disclosure, not evidence of increased repetitions.

E6.justification: The principal vision scores, ablation numbers, and appendix single-task results are retained. v2 adds GLUE averages of 85.30% for the proposed method, 77.77% for NTK linearization, and 73.25% for non-linear fine-tuning, plus efficiency and diagnostic results. The Cars–RESISC45 heatmaps also exchange their representation/classification assignments between v1 Figure 7 and v2 Figure 8.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Proposition 1's data–task-vector orthogonality argument and the subsequent attention-head derivation. The representation-level disentanglement equation survives from Property 4 as Definition 2, while v2 introduces a formal kernel-behavior test requiring equality between non-linear and post-hoc outputs. This substantially revises the mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The main efficiency, task-arithmetic accuracy, and representation-versus-classification-head contributions remain, including the reported 2.38- and 8.37-point advantages. However, v2's abstract replaces the claim that attention-only tuning makes the whole model operate linearly with the more localized claim that attention modules exhibit kernel behavior.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the linear-layer/orthogonality mechanism argument with an empirical kernel-behavior interpretation and emphasizes coefficient robustness. Its discussion adds the requirement for identical architectures and initializations, potential unsupervised applications, and questions concerning attention-block selection and sparsity. The earlier uncertainty about tuning biases remains.

D1.justification: The advertised code location changes from linear_task_arithmetic to task_arithmetic_tangent, and Table 4 adds parameter counts, memory-size information, and training times. Appendix A retains the hardware and core training hyperparameters but removes the statement that no hyperparameter search was performed. Detailed NLP-specific training instructions remain absent.

R1.justification: The related-work section replaces its broad interpolation, fusion, and multitask-learning organization with a pre-merging versus during-merging taxonomy, explicitly positioning the proposed method in the former category. Discussion of TAFT and sparse/subspace merging expands, several earlier research strands disappear, and NLP model and benchmark references are added.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and central argument are extensively rewritten around kernel behavior, individual-model accuracy, the accuracy gap, and coefficient robustness. Terminology changes throughout, the conclusion becomes an expanded discussion, and the cosine-similarity analysis moves to Appendix B.4.

P2.justification: v2 adds a logic-flow diagram, kernel-behavior and coefficient-sensitivity plots, and summary, NLP, and efficiency tables. It redraws the introductory illustration and cosine heatmaps, relocates existing displays, swaps the appendix heatmap rows, and adopts the ICLR layout. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence for comparative efficiency (Table 4), kernel behavior (Figure 3), and coefficient robustness (Figure 9), while improving exposition and stating important applicability limits. The gains are qualified: NLP training details remain sparse, the kernel diagnostic compares accuracy rather than establishing the defined output equality, and revised normalization and ablation descriptions are not reconciled with unchanged scores. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
